sample_unit: radiographic images (each queried six times per model)

links.outcome: LLM accuracy identifying implant level, connection, brand, manufacturer on radiographs versus reference
links.effect: Structural characteristics identified with accuracies of 51.67% to 82.5%; brand and manufacturer recognition 4.17%-32.78%.
links.quote: Structural characteristics (implant level and connection type) were identified with accuracies ranging from 51.67% to 82.5%, whereas brand and manufacturer recognition remained consistently poor (4.17%-32.78%).

links.outcome: Abstention/deferral versus hallucination rates across LLMs on implant identification
links.effect: Hallucinations were >87% of errors in all models; ChatGPT-5 showed higher abstention and lower hallucination frequency.
links.quote: Hallucinations represented the predominant error type (>87% of errors in all models), while ChatGPT-5 showed a comparatively higher rate of abstention and lower hallucination frequency.

links.outcome: Overconfident definitive incorrect responses (hallucinations) among errors
links.effect: Hallucinations (definitive incorrect answers) exceeded 87% of errors in all four models; newer model abstained more often.
links.quote: Hallucinations represented the predominant error type (>87% of errors in all models), while ChatGPT-5 showed a comparatively higher rate of abstention and lower hallucination frequency.

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the accuracy and hallucination/abstention behaviors of multiple multimodal LLMs on dental implant identification using a radiographic image dataset, without testing a specific operational deployment practice or safeguard intervention.
